Deploying High Density Workloads in the Data Center
• Data Centers have finite resources
•
These limited resources create scarcity in the face of demand
•
This drives the need to optimize resource utilization for 
efficiency
• The three main resource constraints are
•
Power
•
Cooling
•
Space
• These resources are interrelated
•
Excess demand on one resource could negatively impact other 
resources
•
These interrelationships can also impact InfiniBand cable lengths

DGX B300 SuperPOD Data Center Infrastructure
•
DGX B300 systems are available in both DC and AC versions
•
For high density deployments ( 4 systems per rack), systems are deployed 
in an MGX style rack, which features an integrated rear DC Busbar and is 
powered by DC Power Shelves, instead of traditional AC Rack PDUs
•
Active Rear Door Heat Exchangers (RDHx) are recommended to help 
manage heat loads in high density deployments
•
Lower density deployments (2 systems per rack) may use traditional AC 
Rack PDUs, and unassisted air cooling.

DGX B300 SuperPOD Data Center Infrastructure
Data Center Deployment Pattern
•
A DGX Scalable Unit (SU) consists of up to 72 
(XDR) or 64 (Spectrum-X) DGX B300 systems
•
A DGX SuperPOD can be comprised of 
multiple Scalable Units, interconnected with 
XDR IB or Spectrum-X as well as Ethernet In-
band and Storage Fabrics, combined with a 
compatible storage system. 
•
Performance and cost optimized
•
High Density and Low-Density Deployment 
options
•
Four air-cooled DGX B300s per 48U MGX rack in 
high density deployment pattern, with Active Rear 
Door Heat Exchangers, or
•
Two traditional air-cooled DGX B300s per 48U/52U 
rack
•
Proximity of the cabinets is governed by 
cable distance limits
•
Compute Fabric  (XDR IB or Spectrum-X) drives 
rack-to-rack cable distance requirements

Planning a data center deployment
Site Assessments and Space Planning
• To prepare for a DGX B300 Deployment, the following 
should be assessed and integrated into the deployment 
plan
• Pre-deployment Site Survey and Space Planning
• Does the site comply with all the operating requirements of 
the equipment?
• Assign and pre-prepare the location where the systems will 
be deployed
• Loading Dock Assessment
• Does the site have a loading dock with hydraulic levelers for 
smooth transition from truck to staging area?
• Staging Space Assessment
• Is there sufficient secure staging space to unpack or uncrate 
the equipment and prepare it for deployment?
• Pathway Assessment
• Ramps, Door Dimensions, Elevators, Turn Radiuses, Etc.
• Assure there are no obstacles that would impede the safe 
and smooth movement of equipment to the deployment area

Planning a data center deployment
Safety
• Assure worker compliance with all safety protocols 
and protective measures
• Use of rack tugs, server lifts, pallet jacks, or other conveyances in 
accordance with manufacturer recommendations
• Use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
• Safety shoes, hard hats, safety glasses, gloves, lumbar support belts
• Hearing protection
• Proper and timely waste disposal
• Personnel Safety Training Program compliance

Planning a data center deployment
Safety
• Where applicable, assure that the following are in place
Leak Detection Systems
Spill Mitigation Training
PG25 Safety Program
PG25 Compliant Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
PG25 Spill Kits
PG25 Storage
Proper PG25 Disposal procedures
Note: Consult with local or national Authorities Having Jurisdiction 
for safety and regulatory requirements when deploying PG25 based 
cooling systems.

Rear Door Heat Exchangers
Overview
• NVIDIA Does not provide or recommend specific RDHx models. Consult with suppliers to assure 
compliance with heat load and airflow requirements
• Passive Rear Door Heat Exchangers are not recommended for DGX B300 Systems
• Rear Door Heat Exchangers (RDHx) units should be installed in accordance with manufacturer 
specifications, and in compliance with all Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs)
• RDHx Design Considerations
• Power Provisioning Requirements
• Floor load calculations
• Containment aisle pitch
• Hot Aisle width and service clearances
• Under floor vs. overhead piping designs
• Supplemental fluid valve controls
• Leak detection system
• CDU placement
• Grounding & Bonding
• Local seismic requirements
Note: The Rear Door Heat Exchanger manufacturer may need to provide a custom mounting bracket for use with the MGX cabinet.

Strategies for Cooling Optimization and Scalability
Environmental Parameters
• Each DGX B300 system requires up to approximately 
2145 CFM of supply air at sea level
• Supply air should generally comply with ASHRAE Class A2 
specifications, but with a maximum supply air temperature 
of 30°C (86°F).
• For optimal cooling efficiency and system 
performance, air contamination should be mitigated 
through filtration
• Minimum of MERV 13 (or EN779-2012 M6/F7, or ISO 16890 
ePM1-50%) rated filter
• Rack area should meet the cleanliness level of the ISO 
14644-1 Class-8 standard 
• Maximum particulate counts not to exceed 3,520,000 @ 0.5 
µm/m3 for longer than 15 minutes.

Cabling
DGX Infrastructure Support 
•
Bundle cables together in groups of relevance (for example, ISL 
(Inter-Switch Link) cables and uplinks to core devices) to ease 
management and troubleshooting.
•
Use cables of correct length.
•
Allow for bend radiuses and intra-rack cable routing in cable 
length calculations
•
Keep cable runs under 90% of the max distance supported for 
each media type, as specified in the applicable standard.
•
Keep copper and fiber bundles and runs separated.
•
Install spare cables in advance for future replacement of 
damaged cables.
•
Use color coding of the cable ties. The colors should indicate the 
endpoints. Place labels at both ends, as well as along the run.
Example of proper cable management

Cabling
DGX Cabling Types 
•
The DGX B300 SuperPOD Compute Fabric is mainly interconnected with MPO12 APC passive single mode fiber 
cables connected to twin port OSFP Transceivers
•
Copper Cat6 Ethernet cables are also used in the Management Network Fabric
•
For maximum performance, cable lengths should be limited to 500 Meters or less.

OSFP Shell Terms
IHS = Integrated Heat Sink – Cooling fins integrated into plug “Finned Top, Twin-Port OSFP”

DR4 = Datacenter Reach (500-meters) 4-channels, parallel into MPO-12/APC optical connectors (4 transmit & 4 receive)
FR4= Far Reach (2km) 4-channels, multiplexed into 2-fiber LC optical connectors (1 transmit & 1 receive)

•
The DGX B300 SuperPOD is a complex system that demands 
significant power and cooling resources
•
Depending on data center site capabilities, this resource 
demand may require adjacent rows to be unutilized or 
underutilized, to aggregate power and cooling resources into 
the SuperPOD rows
•
Successful deployments often rely on careful alignment and 
planning across several organizational and technical domains
